citations.claim: energy still near initial before close encounter
energy begins to drop, distance 0.76, substeps 27
first violation: energy 415.2, delta 140.3 > allowed 74.98, distance 0.465, potential -1665.6, substeps 30 maxed

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.03329 to 0.005 (single field) keeping same 22 steps, G, masses, positions, velocities. Substep budget now sufficient, energy conserved (555.5255 -> 555.5255) with zero violations.

explanation: Two massive bodies (m~11 and 18, G~4.6) approach to 0.46 separation, comparable to softening 0.3, causing potential to plunge from -746 (step20) to -1665 (step22). Leapfrog with dt=0.0333 splits into at most 30 substeps at step22, insufficient to resolve the high acceleration/velocity phase, so total energy falls from 555.5 to 415.2 (delta 140 vs allowed 75). Reducing dt to 0.005 removes the violation with identical initial conditions and steps, proving integration error.
vision_note: Two blue bodies on converging tracks rapidly close from a clear gap in step 19 to near-touching in step 21 and overlapping in step 22. The trajectory from step 22 shows an abrupt kink/overlap indicating a very close, high-acceleration encounter that the integrator struggles to resolve.
